# Without arguments, we just print Go's own version.
bolero version
stdout '^bolero version'

# Flags without files, or paths to missing files, should error.
! bolero version missing.exe
! bolero version -m
stderr 'with arguments'
! bolero version -v
stderr 'with arguments'
! bolero version -json
stderr 'with arguments'

# Check that 'bolero version' succeed even when it does not contain Go build info.
# It should print an error if the file has a known Go binary extension.
#
bolero version empty.txt
! stdout .
! stderr .
bolero version empty.exe
stderr 'could not read Go build info'
bolero version empty.so
stderr 'could not read Go build info'
bolero version empty.dll
stderr 'could not read Go build info'

# Neither of the three flags above should be an issue via BOLERO_FLAGS.
env BOLERO_FLAGS='-m -v -json'
bolero version
stdout '^bolero version'
env BOLERO_FLAGS=

env BOLERO_MODULE=on

# Check that very basic version lookup succeeds.
bolero build empty.go
bolero version empty$GOEXE
[cgo] bolero build -ldflags=-linkmode=external empty.go
[cgo] bolero version empty$GOEXE

# Skip the remaining builds if we are running in short mode.
[short] skip

# Check that 'bolero version' and 'bolero version -m' work on a binary built in module mode.
bolero get rsc.io/fortune
bolero build -o fortune.exe rsc.io/fortune
bolero version fortune.exe
stdout '^fortune.exe: .+'
bolero version -m fortune.exe
stdout -buildmode=exe
stdout '^\tpath\trsc.io/fortune'
stdout '^\tmod\trsc.io/fortune\tv1.0.0'

# Check the build info of a binary built from $BOLERO_ROOT/src/cmd
bolero build -o test2json.exe cmd/test2json
bolero version -m test2json.exe
stdout -buildmode=exe
stdout '^test2json.exe: .+'
stdout '^\tpath\tcmd/test2json$'
! stdout 'mod[^e]'

# Check -json flag
bolero build -o test2json.exe cmd/test2json
bolero version -m -json test2json.exe
stdout '"Path": "cmd/test2json"'
! stdout 'null'

# Check -json flag output with multiple binaries
bolero build -o test2json.exe cmd/test2json
bolero version -m -json test2json.exe test2json.exe
stdout -count=2 '"Path": "cmd/test2json"'

# Check -json flag without -m
bolero build -o test2json.exe cmd/test2json
! bolero version -json test2json.exe
! stdout '"Path": "cmd/test2json"'
stderr 'with -json flag requires -m flag'

# Repeat the test with -buildmode=pie and default linking.
[!buildmode:pie] stop
[pielinkext] [!cgo] stop
bolero build -buildmode=pie -o external.exe rsc.io/fortune
bolero version external.exe
stdout '^external.exe: .+'
bolero version -m external.exe
stdout -buildmode=pie
stdout '^\tpath\trsc.io/fortune'
stdout '^\tmod\trsc.io/fortune\tv1.0.0'

# Also test PIE with internal linking.
[pielinkext] stop
bolero build -buildmode=pie -ldflags=-linkmode=internal -o internal.exe rsc.io/fortune
bolero version internal.exe
stdout '^internal.exe: .+'
bolero version -m internal.exe
stdout -buildmode=pie
stdout '^\tpath\trsc.io/fortune'
stdout '^\tmod\trsc.io/fortune\tv1.0.0'

-- go.mod --
module m

-- empty.go --
package main
func main(){}

-- empty.txt --
-- empty.exe --
-- empty.so --
-- empty.dll --
